chapter123.rule: VERIFIED and IMPLEMENTED. Common Level Range = Average Ratio (Director's Ratio) +/- 15%, MULTIPLICATIVE on the ratio (handbook example: avg 78.00% => lower 66.30%, upper 89.70%). Subject Property Ratio = assessed value / true value as found by the hearing body. If the Subject Property Ratio falls WITHIN the range, NO reduction is made. If it exceeds the upper limit OR falls below the lower limit, the assessment becomes Average Ratio x true value — so falling below the corridor produces an INCREASE, which is the statutory outcome, not merely a risk.
chapter123.statutes: N.J.S.A. 54:1-35a (average ratio); 54:3-22(c) (limits relief the county board may grant); 54:51A-6 (same limit on the Tax Court). Case law: North Brunswick Twp. v. Gochal, 27 N.J. Tax 31 (Tax Ct. 2012).

The deadline extends past April 1 whenever a municipality has not completed bulk mailing at least 45 days before April 1, based on the certification of bulk mailing filed with the county board — the engine has no bulk-mailing date input and cannot model this. May 1 in revaluation/reassessment municipalities VERIFIED.

dependsOn.filingFee: CORRECTED 2026-08-15 to a banded schedule (filingFee.bands, read through filingFeeFor()). N.J.S.A. 54:3-21.3; N.J.A.C. 18:12A-1.6(d) and 1.7: under $150,000 = $5; $150,000 to <$500,000 = $25; $500,000 to <$1,000,000 = $100; $1,000,000 or more = $150. The engine models valuation appeals only, so those cases are out of scope rather than wrong.

Also unencoded: appeal from a county board judgment to the Tax Court is due within 45 days of the judgment's mailing.

_knownGap: KNOWN-GAP GAP-052: the 45-day bulk-mailing extension cannot be computed. N.J.S.A. 54:3-21 makes the deadline April 1 OR 45 days from the mailing of the Notification of Assessment, whichever is later, extended whenever a municipality has not completed bulk mailing at least 45 days before April 1. The engine has no bulk-mailing date input, so a homeowner in a late-mailing municipality is shown April 1 when they in fact have longer. Rule VERIFIED; input missing.

KNOWN-GAP GAP-051: weekend/holiday rollover is not modelled in deadline.ts. Handbook §1105.01: if the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday the deadline is the first business day thereafter. See /KNOWN-GAPS.md.
appealWindow.opens: when the annual assessment notice (postcard) mails, typically by February 1
appealWindow.deadlineRule: April 1, or 45 days after the bulk mailing of assessment notices, whichever is later. May 1 in municipalities undergoing a district-wide revaluation or reassessment. [PARTIALLY VERIFIED — April 1, the 45-day rule and the May 1 revaluation deadline are confirmed; the engine has no bulk-mailing date input, so it cannot compute the extended deadline]
appealWindow.filingCutoffNote: The Bergen County Board of Taxation must have your petition in hand by the deadline. Mailing it that day is not enough — a postmark does not count, and a petition that arrives late is dismissed without a hearing. [VERIFIED — NJ Assessors Handbook §1105.01: "The word 'filed' has been interpreted by the courts to mean received in the office of the County Board of Taxation by April 1. A postmark of a mailed petition is not sufficient."]

filingFee.waiverConditions: The statutory fee is banded by assessed value: $5 under $150,000; $25 from $150,000 to under $500,000; $100 from $500,000 to under $1,000,000; $150 at $1,000,000 or more. No fee is charged on an appeal from the denial of a veteran, surviving-spouse, senior/disabled or disabled-veteran deduction or exemption. [VERIFIED — N.J.S.A. 54:3-21.3; N.J.A.C. 18:12A-1.6(d) and 1.7, per NJ Assessors Handbook §1105.04. The deduction/exemption waiver is not modelled: the engine handles valuation appeals only.]

evidenceStandard: Comparable arm's-length sales valued as at October 1 of the pre-tax year. New Jersey then applies the Chapter 123 common level range: the county board compares your assessment-to-true-value ratio against your municipality's average ratio ±15%, and inside that range it may grant no reduction at all. Below the range it must raise the assessment. [PARTIALLY VERIFIED — the October 1 valuation date and the Chapter 123 test are confirmed (Handbook §§1105.18–1105.20). Chapter 123 is the governing but not the exclusive discrimination remedy (North Brunswick Twp. v. Gochal, 27 N.J. Tax 31). The 'up to five comparables' and 24-month recency figures are UNSOURCED and have been dropped from this sentence; the taxpayer-side 7-day evidence rule is UNCONFIRMED (N.J.A.C. 18:12A-1.9 not fetched).]
